notes:
ACCESS: reachable, no wall on the pages that matter. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 on every /browse/ category page on the first or second fingerprint; ~50 requests over the session with probe.py's 2s/host pacing, no 403 and no 429. TWO exceptions worth recording: https://www.samsclub.com/sitemap.xml serves a "Let us know you're not a robot" interstitial (so the sitemap route is walled and was ABANDONED - the tree came from the site's own page payloads instead), and https://www.samsclub.com/b/bath/1444 resolves to an unrelated 'Grocery' page, so the /b/ URL form was not used. MEMBERSHIP: Sam's Club gates purchase and some pricing behind membership, but category browsing and product counts are public - I was never asked to sign in and never hit a paywall.
ROBOTS (https://www.samsclub.com/robots.txt, fetched FIRST, HTTP 200, 448 bytes): a single 'User-agent: *' group. NO ClaudeBot, NO anthropic-ai, NO Claude-Web, NO Claude-SearchBot, and no literal 'Claude' string anywhere (checked per the galerieslafayette lesson). Disallows are *SCDC=1*, /*?bvroute, /lists/, */samsclub/0, /checkout/, /cart, /search, /pharmacy/login/, /tracking, /midas/, /buy-it-again, /account, /orders, /r/, /login, /reviews/write-review; plus 'Allow: /ads.txt'. The /browse/<slug>/<id> category paths I used are NOT disallowed. Compliance record: I requested no /search URL, no SCDC=1, no bvroute, no /r/ short link and no account or checkout path. The only query parameter used was ?page=N, which is not disallowed. No Crawl-delay is declared. Per-host discipline: every request went to www.samsclub.com; no API host, CDN or third party was contacted, because the counts and the tree are both server-rendered into the page's own __NEXT_DATA__.
TREE: taken from the site's OWN navigation payload, not guessed and not from URL shape. Each /browse/ page embeds a Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ blob whose contentLayout carries the department's child links, so the tree was walked top-down from Home (/browse/Home/1285, 1,889 items) -> Bath (/browse/Bath/10220126, 143). Bath's own payload declares exactly EIGHT children plus a Shop All: Shop All Bath (12170105), Bath Accessories (10270125), Bath Mats (1963), Bath Towels (1438) with its child Beach Towels (4190103), Bath Tubs (13910187), Showers & Bathtubs (1422), Toilets (10220130) and Vanities & Bathroom Furniture (1439). The adjacent departments were then walked to make sure nothing bathroom-shaped was hiding outside Bath: Home Improvement (1390, 1,034) -> Bath & Kitchen Renovation (2360175), Plumbing (1420), Bathroom Lighting (1340147); Home Decor (1358, 238) -> Mirrors (1370); Household Essentials -> Cleaning Supplies -> Bathroom Cleaners (360211). All six were opened and enumerated and all six are in review[] with the reason they are not rows. Sam's Club has NO bathroom mirror node, NO bathroom-storage node, NO basin/sink node beyond one utility sink, and NO standalone taps node - it is a warehouse club with a narrow bathroom range.
URL FORM AND CANONICALS: Sam's Club resolves a /browse/ URL by its trailing numeric id and treats the slug as cosmetic, so the SAME node answers to several slugs. Every recorded link is the URL the page's own rel=canonical declares: Bath Accessories canonicalises to /browse/bath-accessories-bathroom-accessories/10270125 (not the /Bath-Accessories/ form in the nav) and Showers & Bathtubs canonicalises to /browse/shower-fixtures/1422 (not /Showers-%26-Bathtubs/1422). Both the nav form and the canonical form of every node were run through the dedup index. One genuine oddity is documented in review: node 1963, whose H1 is 'Bath Mats', declares rel=canonical /browse/embroidery/1963 - a wrong slug on Sam's Club's side.
QTY - SOURCE AND PROOF. Source: searchResult.aggregatedCount in the PLP's own __NEXT_DATA__, which equals itemStacks[0].meta.totalItemCount, equals itemStacks[0].count, and equals the number the site renders in its own H1 (meta.totalItemCountDisplay, e.g. 'Bath(143+)'). The rendered H1 string is LOSSY - it appends a '+' - so the payload figure was used and the H1 is the cross-check, which is the Wayfair situation from BATCH_BRIEF s3 (payload exact, rendered string lossy). PROOF BY ENUMERATION TO EXHAUSTION, run on all 14 nodes touched: each was paginated with ?page=N to its declared paginationV2.maxPage and every product tile's usItemId collected, excluding non-product tiles (MarqueeDisplayAd) and counting sponsored tiles. aggregatedCount was matched EXACTLY by the distinct id count on five nodes - Bath Towels 20/20, Bath Tubs 4/4, Showers & Bathtubs 25/25, Toilets 22/22, Vanities 30/30 - all five being nodes with ZERO sponsored tiles. On the nodes where the enumeration came up short the shortfall tracks the sponsored-tile count exactly: Bath Accessories 23 vs 25 with 2 sponsored, Bath Mats 13 vs 15 with 2 sponsored, Beach Towels 12 vs 13. Sponsored placements displace organic slots in the rendered grid without reducing the catalogue total, which is why aggregatedCount is the right figure and the grid scrape is not. PAGINATION WAS VERIFIED REAL, not the IKEA trap: on the 4-page Bath node pages 1-4 returned 44/47/47/8 products with 44/45/45/6 NEW ids each time, so ?page=N genuinely advances. maxPage also reconciles with the totals (143 over 4 pages, 106 over 3, 58 over 2, everything <=46 over 1). Counts were re-read on separate fetches with separate fingerprints and did not move (143, 25, 25, 22 both times). NO estimate, NO parent figure reused for a child, NO sibling sums.
VERIFICATION: the three recorded counts discriminate against the wider set actually measured (143 / 106 / 58 / 30 / 25 / 25 / 22 / 20 / 19 / 17 / 15 / 13 / 10 / 4 - no site-wide constant). Bath Accessories and Showers & Bathtubs both happen to be 25, and that was checked rather than assumed: their product-id sets overlap by only 4 of 25, so they are genuinely different nodes that coincidentally have the same size. Every node's H1 was read and matched the node requested. CONTAINMENT was proved by usItemId set for every parent/child claim, not asserted: all eight children are strict subsets of the Bath department, and Bath Tubs is a strict subset of Showers & Bathtubs (4 of 4 in, 0 out), which is why Bath Tubs is withheld.
ROWS AND CLASSIFICATION: three leaves. Bath Accessories (25) is Bathroom under rules 13/17 - internal product types are Shower Curtains & Liners 4, Showerheads & Handheld Showers 4, Towel Warmers 3, Face Mirrors 2, Bath Accessories Sets 2, plus a Faucet, a Bidet, a Toilet Lid & Tank Cover, a Bath Rug, a Towel, a Ventilation Fan, an Air Purifier and a Body Fat Analyzer. DISCLOSED IMPURITY: the air purifier and the body-fat scale are not Bathroom under rule 3, and the 4 shower curtains would be Textile under rule 20 - but they are 6 of 25 in a node whose name, parentage and dominant product type are all bathroom accessories, and the site offers no sub-node to split them, so the node is recorded whole and the mixture is stated. Showers & Bathtubs (25) is Bathroom under rules 5/6/7 - Showerheads & Handheld Showers 7, Shower Doors 4, Shower Bases 4, Bathtubs 3, Shower Enclosures 2, Shower Stalls 2, plus a sink, a faucet and a pet shower attachment. Toilets (22) is Bathroom under rules 4/14 - Bidet Toilet Seats 9, Toilets 2, Bidets 2, Toilet Seats 2, Toilet Brushes & Holders 2, Toilet Paper Holders 1, Bidet Attachments 1, Toilet Lid & Tank Covers 1, plus a faucet and a drain tool. The Bath department node itself is the grouping row with blank qty and blank link under rule 24.
DEDUP (OPTION 1, URL-exact index): already_extracted() was run on all 20 candidate, canonical, nav-form and id-only URL variants. ONE HIT, and it is the decisive one for this company - /browse/vanities-bathroom-furniture/1439 is in Furniture.xlsx as 'Vanities & Bathroom Furniture', so Sam's Club's 30-product bathroom vanity node (27 of them internally typed 'Bathroom Vanities') STAYS IN FURNITURE and is in review[], never rows[], exactly as the OPTION 1 decision requires. samsclub.com carries 24 Furniture.xlsx records in total; the other 23 are sofas, beds, dressers, dining, office and patio, none bathroom. Final.xlsx does not cover samsclub.com. Blind spots worked: (a) canonicals - both the nav slug and the rel=canonical slug of every node were index-checked separately, and the id-only form /browse/1439 was checked too since Furniture.xlsx itself holds an id-only Sam's Club URL (/browse/1371); (b)/(c) locale - samsclub.com is a single-locale US storefront with no locale prefix and no cross-host hreflang alternate, and Furniture.xlsx used the identical /browse/ form; (d) one page two nav paths - Bath Accessories, Bath Tubs, Showers & Bathtubs, Toilets and Bathroom Lighting are each reachable from BOTH the Home > Bath tree AND the Home Improvement > Bath & Kitchen Renovation tree at identical URLs; each is one record under rule 28 and the Home Improvement roll-up is withheld.
EXCLUDED and why, in one place: Vanities & Bathroom Furniture -> already extracted (Furniture). Bath Tubs -> proven strict subset of a recorded sibling. Shop All Bath -> rule 25 plus partial roll-up. Bath & Kitchen Renovation -> cross-department roll-up overlapping 49 of the recorded products. Bath Towels, Beach Towels, Bath Mats -> Textile (rules 15/16/20). Bathroom Lighting -> Lighting (rules 11/19). Bathroom Cleaners -> consumable cleaning chemicals under Household Essentials, not bathroom accessories. Home Decor > Mirrors -> decorative and bedroom mirrors, and the site's two lighted vanity mirrors are already inside the recorded Bath Accessories leaf. Plumbing -> water coolers and heaters, not sanitaryware. No empty nodes were found: every node opened returned a populated grid. One structural gap is on the record in review[]: five products (four OVE Decors sliding shower doors and one hair towel) sit in the Bath department under no child and are therefore counted in no row.

Department distinct usItemId set = 140 (aggregatedCount reads 141; the 1-unit gap is a single sponsored tile, consistent with the sponsored-tile behavior documented earlier in notes). Union of the 8 children's distinct usItemId sets = 135 (Vanities & Bathroom Furniture 29, Bath Accessories 23, Showers & Bathtubs 26, Toilets 22, Bath Towels 20, Bath Mats 13, Beach Towels 12, Bath Tubs 4 - all individually deduplicated against each other, e.g. Bath Tubs' 4 ids are the same 4 already inside Showers & Bathtubs). Department-set minus union-of-children-set = exactly 5 residue ids, an EXACT reproduction of the original run's finding (same 5 usItemIds, same 5 names, re-identified independently by live set subtraction rather than trusted from the prior note): 4 OVE Decors frameless sliding shower doors (usItemId 18043761120 'Selby 55-1/2-60W x 74H', 18058555320 'Selby 45-1/16-48W x 74H', 18055068798 'Selby 67-1/2-72W x 74H', 18045565583 'Bel 70-3/16-72-3/16W x 78-3/4H Soft-Close'; internal type 'Shower Doors' on all 4) plus 1 'NIGHT Quick Dry Hair Towel' (usItemId 15216571941, internal type 'Towels & Washcloths'). The 4 shower doors sit in the Bath department under no child node and have no listing URL of their own; they are unambiguously Bathroom under rule 7 (Enclosures & Screens - Shower Doors explicitly listed), so this qty=4 leaf carries them, using the department's own URL under the same OPTION applied to Kmart (a '(other)' leaf at the parent URL when genuine residue exists with no deeper listing URL). The 5th residue item, the hair towel, is EXCLUDED from this row's qty: it is Textile (Towels & Washcloths, rule 20), not Bathroom, so it is not fabricated into this count; it remains noted for completeness only. No other candidate URL (product-detail or otherwise) exists for these 4 products, so no separate rows[] URL could be recorded per rule 27 - the department URL is used exactly as the Kmart precedent used its own parent URLs. Cross-checked cross_category_url_index.json for 'shower-door', 'OVE Decors', 'Selby' and 'hair-towel' before recording: only unrelated 'hair-towel' substring hits elsewhere in the index (a different company's URL slug), no samsclub.com hit, so no dedup applies.
